content.text:
The Evidence and Structure pages now have a **Spread** slider and ways to fly through the 3D view. The slider and zooming work in the browser; flying and the reset button still need you to try them.

I checked with the two other sessions first. Neither was touching these files, and their notes on how to avoid conflicts are followed. I've told them I'm finished.

**Spread slider (bottom centre, 1× to 4×)**
- It pushes everything further apart, while the dots, halos, diamonds and labels grow only a little. So the gaps open up instead of everything just getting bigger.
- The camera pulls back with it, so the view stays framed. You then zoom into the area you want.
- On Structure at 3.1×, clusters separated clearly and far fewer theme labels were hidden by overlaps.
- Your chosen spread is remembered in your browser.

**Why zooming sometimes didn't work, and the fix**
- Zoom always aimed at the centre of the universe and stopped 2.2 units from it, so you couldn't get any closer.
- Now the scroll wheel zooms toward whatever is under your mouse and can go much closer. This also works with the pointer over a label.

**Moving back and forth**
- **W / S** flies forward and back, **A / D** moves sideways, and **Q / E** moves down and up. Hold **Shift** to go faster. The arrow keys still switch checkpoints.
- Right-drag (or Shift-drag) pans the view.
- The pad has hold-to-fly forward/back buttons and a **Reset view** button that glides back to the starting view.

**Checked so far:** the type-check passes. In the browser, the slider, zoom-toward-cursor and zoom over labels all worked. W/S flying and the reset glide are untested: the test Chrome window was in the background, so animation was frozen. Please try those two yourself; if they don't move, it's in `navigate.tsx`.

The new code is in `web/src/screens/scan/navigate.tsx`, with smaller changes in `Scene.tsx`, `Scan.tsx`, `scan.css` and `StructureLayer.tsx`. I added a session-log line to `foundation/STATE.md`. Nothing is committed. One session pointed out that some older uncommitted changes in `scan.css` aren't theirs, so check that file's diff before committing.

## D-043 — Structure & context: classify → cluster → contextualize → elicit, per checkpoint
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan (fresh extraction; evidence graph in SQLite with RAG; page 2 "collapse into structure"; "spawn sub agents to find optimizations … I want to see improvements with the new data"), designed from three read-only reviews (classification, clustering, contextualize), implemented by agent · Status: accepted
- Decision (code in `src/bmw_req/structure/`, every stage a `checkpoint_run`; cp2 builds on cp1):
  1. **classify** (`classify.py`, extract-v4): fixed ~45-aspect taxonomy shared by all sources (`taxonomy.py`); intensity (1–3) separate from impact; nature/want_kind/occupant/context/benchmark/future_cue/explicit; one signal per (aspect, nature); hints for Source C self-reported severity and the Source D survey prompt (never quoted); quotes ≥ 4 words; ~2.6k-token cacheable prompt; 20 comments per luna Flex call. cp2 classifies only the delta. A/B on a fixed 400-comment sample (`scripts/benchmark_classify.py`, `data/eval/classify_ab.json`): BMW-label macro 0.609 → 0.615, likes 0.84 → 0.90, "serious" → high 0.17 → 0.37, "minor" → low 0.22 → 0.49, quotes < 4 words 13 % → 5 %, survey-prompt quotes 10 → 0, Korea in-scope 0.71 → 0.76, aspect coverage 0 → 99 %; wants 0.56 → 0.54 (≈). `classify_context.py`: study rows (|z| ≥ 0.8 → gap/like), research (luna: aspect + nature), options (aspect) into `source_aspect`.
  2. **cluster** (`cluster.py`): portfolio-wide within polarity × category, average linkage 0.35 + recursive split of oversized clusters; stable keys `cl:<pol>:<cat>:<anchor>`; cp2 assigns new signals to cp1 clusters (mean-member cosine ≤ 0.35), clusters only leftovers; track weight = comment share, strengthened/weakened only if ≥ 10 % relative AND |z| ≥ 1.96 (the random JAN/JUL split must not look like change).
  3. **contextualize** (`contextualize.py`): luna standardizes one insight per cluster (title, statement, need type, quality issue, product decision); duplicate judge on cosine ≥ 0.86 pairs; themes (average linkage 0.45 on statement embeddings, cp2 joins nearest cp1 theme ≥ 0.55); RAG: research/study/options embedded once (`node_embedding`), per theme top-k checkpoint-visible candidates verified by luna into typed `evidence_edge`s (supports, contradicts, competes_with, trend_for, available_as_option, context). cp2 re-runs only changed clusters/themes; clean ones carry their edges as held.
  4. **areas** (`areas.py`): this step structures, it does not draft requirements (Atahan: drafting proposals is the next step). sol groups the themes into 15–40 potential requirement areas (title, need, kind improve / keep / emerging, why now from the given evidence, ≤ 3 open questions for drafting); code adds comments, line × market coverage and evidence counts; quality-only themes form a separate quality list. cp2 keeps area keys, attaches new themes, records change notes; tracks significance-tested. `elicit.py` (candidate drafting with code checks: future horizon needs a dated trend edge, own-market evidence per target, cited ids from the theme's edges) is kept for the next step and not run here.
  5. **Page 2 "Structure"** (`/structure`, same canvas as the scan): comments morph into their clusters; cluster nodes (blue improve / white keep; dot held, ring new, double ring strengthened, amber weakened/lost), theme halos, requirement-area diamonds above their themes, evidence arcs to the exact ring items; stage funnel; live agent panel (stages, progress, feed of AI steps from the audit trail; comments flash as they are classified); inspectors for clusters (signals with quotes), themes (evidence by relation) and areas (need, why now, open questions, coverage); "What the AI found" on comments and research on page 1. API `api/routers/structure.py`.
- Consequences: the old pipeline (`pipeline/`, extract-v3, findings, requirements, linker) stays for history but the new screens read only D-043 tables. Q-021 (over-linking) and the D-038 defect rule are enforced in code here.

"""Stage `cluster` (D-043): comment signals → clusters, checkpoint-incremental, deterministic (no LLM).

Design (clustering review 2026-10-11):
- Portfolio-wide within (polarity × category): polarity `like` vs `improve` (everything else). Twins across car lines
  share one cluster; per car line × market counts live in the payload (D-011 markets stay apart, D-042 5 Series).
- cp1: average-linkage agglomerative clustering, cosine distance 0.35, plus a recursive split of oversized clusters
  (> 15 % of the group and > 60 signals; threshold −0.05 per level, depth ≤ 3) against chaining into "like" blobs.
- Stable keys: `cl:<polarity>:<category-slug>:<anchor signal id>` — the anchor is the medoid at birth, never moved.
- cp2 (parent = cp1 run): each newly visible signal joins the cp1 cluster of its group with the smallest mean cosine
  distance to the members, if ≤ 0.35; leftovers are clustered among themselves into new clusters.
- Tracks per cluster: weight = share of the visible in-scope comment base; strengthened / weakened only if the cp2
  delta share differs from the cp1 share by ≥ 10 % relative AND |z| ≥ 1.96 (two-proportion test); else held.
  A random split must not look like change.

"""

"""Stage `contextualize` (D-043): clusters → standardized insights → themes → evidence graph, per checkpoint.

1. Standardize (luna, batches): one insight per cluster with ≥ 3 comments — title, need statement, need type,
   quality-issue flag, whether a product decision is possible. cp2 re-standardizes only new / strengthened /
   weakened clusters; held clusters carry their cp1 insight.
2. Duplicates: insight pairs with statement-embedding cosine ≥ 0.86 → luna judge → `duplicate_of` / `sub_need_of`.
3. Themes: insights grouped by meaning within their category (complete linkage on statement embeddings, 0.35 —
   average linkage at 0.45 collapsed every category into one theme); luna names each theme. cp2: a new insight joins
   the nearest cp1 theme if cosine ≥ 0.65, else forms a new theme.
4. Connect evidence (RAG): embed research, study items and options once (`node_embedding`); per theme retrieve the
   nearest checkpoint-visible candidates per type, then luna verifies each link with a relation and a reason.
5. Every edge is an `evidence_edge` row with its run id; tracks per insight, theme and edge show what cp2 changed.

`uv run python -m bmw_req.structure.contextualize --checkpoint cp1` (then cp2)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from typing import Literal

import numpy as np
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
"""Stage `areas` (D-043): themes + evidence graph → potential requirement AREAS, per checkpoint.

This stage structures, it does not draft requirements (that is the next step). sol groups the themes into areas a

cp2 passes the cp1 areas: the model keeps them, attaches new themes, and records a change note where an area moved;
keys stay stable so tracks show new / held / strengthened / weakened / lost.

`uv run python -m bmw_req.structure.areas --checkpoint cp1` (then cp2)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json

lastPrompt: what is the difference between classify, cluster, context and areas in the structure page

content.text:
They are four steps in a row, and each one makes the previous step's output smaller and more abstract. The counts along the top of the Structure page show this: **15,043 signals → 400 clusters → 107 themes → 40 areas** (at the JUL 26 checkpoint).

**1. Classify: comment → signals** (`structure/classify.py`, cheap model)
- Each customer comment is read on its own and broken into **signals**. A signal is one statement about one topic, e.g. "the rear seat is too cramped on long trips."
- Each signal gets an **aspect** from a fixed list of about 45 customer-facing topics. The customer study, web research and option list are tagged with the same list, so all sources speak the same language.
- Each signal also gets its type (complaint, praise or wish), how strongly it's said (1–3), a quote, and some context.
- One comment can produce several signals.

**2. Cluster: signals → clusters** (`structure/cluster.py`, plain maths, no AI model)
- Signals that say nearly the same thing are grouped by text similarity.
- Praise and complaints are never mixed, and grouping stays within one category. It spans all models, so the same complaint about the 5 Series and the 7 Series lands in one cluster; per-model and per-market counts are kept.
- This is the moment on the page where the comments fly into their cluster dots. Blue = something to improve, white = something to keep.

**3. Context (contextualize): clusters → insights → themes → evidence links** (`structure/contextualize.py`, cheap model)
- Every cluster with at least 3 comments gets a clean **insight**: a title, a need statement, and whether it's a quality defect or something a product decision can fix.
- Duplicate insights are detected, and related insights are grouped into **themes**. Themes are the halos around groups of clusters.
- For each theme, it searches the research, study and option items and has the model confirm each link as supports, contradicts, competes with, trend for, or available as option. These are the arcs from a theme down to the rings.

**4. Areas: themes → potential requirement areas** (`structure/areas.py`, stronger model)
- Themes are grouped into areas a product manager would recognise, like "Rear-seat comfort on long trips." Areas are the diamonds floating above their themes.
- Each area gets:
  - the underlying need
  - a kind: improve, keep, or emerging expectation
  - why it matters now, citing the linked evidence
  - up to 3 open questions
- Code then adds the hard numbers: comment counts, which car lines and markets it covers, and evidence counts.
- Themes that are only quality defects go to a separate quality list instead of becoming areas.
- This step only structures. Writing actual requirements is the next step (`elicit.py` exists but hasn't been run).

**Across both checkpoints:** the July run builds on the January one. It classifies only the new comments, adds them to the existing clusters, themes and areas, and marks each one as held, new, strengthened, weakened or lost. "Strengthened" and "weakened" are only shown when the change passes a statistical test, so random noise doesn't look like a trend.

Hovering a stage name in the bottom-left Agent panel on the Structure page now shows a short explanation of that stage. I checked it in the browser: hovering Classify, Cluster, Context and Areas each showed the right text.

- **Classify:** reads every comment and splits it into signals: one point about one topic, tagged with one of about 45 shared aspects, plus gap/like/wish, a strength of 1–3 and a quote. Study, research and options get the same aspects.

- **Context:** writes one clean need per cluster, merges look-alikes and groups them into themes (the halos). Then it links each theme to the research, study and option items that support or contradict it (the arcs).
- **Areas:** groups themes into requirement areas a product manager would recognise (the diamonds), with the need, the kind, why now and open questions. Pure quality defects go to a separate list. These aren't requirements yet.

- While you hover, the text replaces the activity feed and the panel doesn't change size, so the stage bar stays under your mouse.
- Keyboard users can Tab to a stage to see the same text.
